request:
SYNTHETIC PLANWORK RECOVERY FIXTURE. Prepare the Aster Charts import coordinator engineering handoff from the two pinned synthetic READMEs. The consumer will turn each plan string into a separate release checklist item and match the exact leading ID. Each item needs its own string and measurable effects. Combine wording within each string to keep the plan compact.

Use these ten change IDs in the changes array, in this order. Define concrete pseudocode or a state transition for each ID, a named owner and a failure invariant. Value-level details matter because the implementer will copy them into assertions.

C01 CANONICALIZE: shared parser normalizes UID via trim and ASCII lowercasing, schemaVersion sets the decoder, original title stays untouched, unresolved datasource tokens survive without substitution.
C02 PREVIEW: revision snapshot and normalized payload fingerprint are captured after validation; tokens return sorted; catalog and activity counts remain the same; preview and UI models share the snapshot.
C03 VALIDATE: report missing title, unsupported version, duplicate panels, malformed expressions as distinct typed faults; return field paths; leave storage untouched.
C04 CONFIRM: share requestId and expectedRevision between iOS/macOS; compute stable fingerprint before receipt access, reject preview cancellation and avoid stale persisted work.
C05 DEDUPE: recover original committed UID, revision and event ID for matching fingerprint; mismatched replay returns RequestConflict; read-only replay before revision comparison.
C06 COMPARE: transaction reads local revision, compares preview revision and advances only once; when the precondition fails include expectedRevision and actualRevision.
C07 ATOMIC: dashboard rows, datasource placeholders, receipt and activity append share one transaction; rollback failures at each boundary; success returns canonical fields.
C08 ROLLBACK: StoreUnavailable returns typed retry outcome; after rollback verify revision, activity and receipts are unchanged; retry original request safely.
C09 UX: both shells expose PreviewReady, StalePreview, Committed, StoreUnavailable; cancellation discards revision and view state; stale requires explicit refresh and confirm.
C10 OBSERVE: low-cardinality counts for stale, duplicate, invalid, rollback, success; no raw dashboard or datasource names; staged rollout with rollback and schema migration observation.

Use these eight verification IDs in the verification array, one string per ID, in this order. Give an executable test description with exact seed, action sequence, an assertion on revision/counts/identity, UI outcome and a final negative check. Give each case enough independent assertion statements that no other case is needed to implement it.

V01 PREVIEW: R4, UID ' ALPHA ', panels CPU and Memory, placeholders metrics-east and metrics-west; preview twice across shells, cancel one.
V02 VALIDATE: existing UID alpha at R4; try invalid schemaVersion 99, empty title and duplicate two panels; correct them incrementally without confirming.
V03 INSTALL: alpha absent at R4, request SYN01 confirms same preview once; observe R5, normalized UID, unchanged raw title, two unresolved placeholders, one receipt and one activity.
V04 STALE: two previews at R4, SYN02 installs before SYN03 confirms; verify the conflict and forced refresh, then a different request SYN04 can confirm R5.
V05 REPLAY: R4 initially, SYN05 commits then its HTTP response is lost; SYN06 commits latest data; SYN05 is replayed twice with its original fingerprint, then with changed panel content.
V06 RACE: two threads use R4 and distinct request IDs for same UID; one transaction wins; both original completions and a subsequent receipt read must agree with resulting revision, catalog row, and activity.
V07 ROLLBACK: fail at dashboard insert, activity append and receipt persist in three isolated seeds; assert no partial effects and simulate a successful retry from R4 with original request.
V08 CROSS_PLATFORM: same eight synthetic samples in independent stores, compare parity of canonical UID, panel references, normalized messages, revision, counts, and stable receipt identity shape.

Implementation rows should each be a concise 220–340 characters. Verification rows should each be 300–420 characters. Descriptive text after each ID is expected, in a form suitable for direct conversion to assertions. Keep goal/gaps/title short. Reference only the pinned inputs. Put exact IDs box/charts:README.md and box/native-apple:README.md in citations. Use null for issueTemplate and issueBody. Aim for about 1,200 to 1,500 total output tokens and leave space for complete JSON.
